food_recommendations.name: Raisin Nut Trail Mix

food_recommendations.name: Beetroot Juice
food_recommendations.preparation: Blend 1 medium raw beet (200 g) with 150 ml water. Strain to get 250 ml juice. Drink before breakfast.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: Beetroot contains dietary nitrates, converting to nitric oxide, relaxing blood vessels, improving flow, reducing vascular resistance.
food_recommendations.evidence: Meta-analyses show systolic BP down 3.5 to 5 mmHg; diastolic 1–2 mmHg within 3 h to weeks (PMC6316347).

food_recommendations.name: Raw Garlic Clove
food_recommendations.preparation: Crush 1 small raw clove (3 g), let rest for 10 min, swallow with water or mix in yogurt.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: Garlic's allicin enhances nitric oxide, inhibits angiotensin II, reduces oxidative stress, improves vessel flexibility.
food_recommendations.evidence: Meta-analysis shows systolic BP down 4.4 mmHg, diastolic 2.7–5.5 mmHg in hypertension (PMC6966103).

food_recommendations.name: Hibiscus Tea
food_recommendations.preparation: Steep 1 tsp dried hibiscus petals in 250 ml hot water for 10 min. Drink 1–2 cups/day.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: Anthocyanins and polyphenols inhibit ACE, reduce oxidative damage, support endothelial function.
food_recommendations.evidence: RCTs show systolic BP down 7 mmHg over weeks. Acts as natural ACE inhibitor (Journal of Nutrition, 2010).

food_recommendations.name: Pomegranate Juice
food_recommendations.preparation: Drink 125 ml unsweetened juice daily.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: Punicalagins and anthocyanins improve endothelial function, reduce inflammation, inhibit ACE, enhance arterial elasticity.
food_recommendations.evidence: Reduces systolic BP and arterial wall thickness after 1 year (Atherosclerosis, 2001).

food_recommendations.name: Soaked Almonds
food_recommendations.preparation: Soak 6–8 raw almonds overnight, peel and eat in the morning.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: Magnesium acts as a calcium channel blocker, reducing vascular resistance.
food_recommendations.evidence: Nut intake lowers BP by 3–5 mmHg (systolic) due to magnesium and healthy fats (Circulation, DASH study).

food_recommendations.name: Oats with Berries
food_recommendations.quantity: ½ cup oats + ¼ cup berries/day
food_recommendations.preparation: Cook ½ cup oats; top with ¼ cup berries (blueberries or strawberries). Eat warm.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: Soluble fiber and antioxidants lower BP and improve vascular health.
food_recommendations.evidence: Soluble fiber and antioxidants linked to BP reduction.

food_recommendations.name: Avocado
food_recommendations.preparation: Eat ½ ripe avocado daily (on toast or salad).
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: Monounsaturated fat and potassium associated with BP reduction.
food_recommendations.evidence: Rich in potassium, supports BP reduction.

food_recommendations.name: Flaxseed Powder
food_recommendations.preparation: Mix 1 tbsp ground flaxseed into yogurt, smoothie, or porridge.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: Omega-3 ALA and lignans reduce systolic BP.
food_recommendations.evidence: Meta-studies link omega-3 ALA to systolic BP reduction by a few mmHg.

food_recommendations.name: Spinach Soup
food_recommendations.preparation: Blend 1 cup cooked spinach with low-sodium broth; season lightly.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: High in dietary nitrates and potassium, comparable to beet juice effects.
food_recommendations.evidence: Nitrates and potassium linked to BP reduction.

food_recommendations.name: Coconut Water
food_recommendations.preparation: Drink 250 ml fresh coconut water.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: Provides potassium and magnesium, acts as a natural diuretic, reduces fluid and BP.
food_recommendations.evidence: Modest BP-lowering effect (West Indian Medical Journal, 2005).

food_recommendations.name: Banana with Peanut Butter Toast
food_recommendations.quantity: 1 slice whole grain toast + 1 medium banana + 1 tbsp peanut butter
food_recommendations.preparation: Toast bread, spread peanut butter, slice banana on top.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: Calorie-dense with complex carbs, healthy fats, potassium. Supports hormone production, brain health.
food_recommendations.evidence: Nutrients (2018): Healthy fats improve hormonal balance, weight gain in underweight.

food_recommendations.name: Full-fat Yogurt with Dates
food_recommendations.quantity: 150–200 g plain full-fat yogurt + 2 chopped dates
food_recommendations.preparation: Mix and consume chilled.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: Full-fat dairy supports calorie intake, vitamin absorption, gut health. Dates add sugar, minerals.
food_recommendations.evidence: American Journal of Clinical Nutrition (2015): Full-fat dairy linked to better metabolic profiles.

food_recommendations.name: Sweet Potato with Olive Oil
food_recommendations.quantity: 1 medium boiled/baked sweet potato + 1 tsp extra virgin olive oil
food_recommendations.preparation: Drizzle oil over cooked sweet potato, season with salt and pepper.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: Complex carbs replenish glycogen, olive oil’s oleic acid supports hormone production, brain health.
food_recommendations.evidence: PREDIMED Study, The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology (2014): Olive oil supports healthy weight.

food_recommendations.name: Feta Cheese and Brown Rice Bowl
food_recommendations.quantity: 50 g feta cheese + ½ cup brown rice + veggies
food_recommendations.preparation: Sauté veggies, mix with cooked rice, add salt and feta cheese on top, stir and enjoy.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: High protein, fat in paneer aid muscle maintenance, lean mass. Brown rice adds fiber, steady energy.
food_recommendations.evidence: Clinical Nutrition: Dairy protein increases lean body mass, body fat in undernourished.

food_recommendations.name: Dry Fruits and Coconut
food_recommendations.quantity: 1 ladoo (1 tbsp desiccated coconut + 3–4 chopped almonds + 2 dates)
food_recommendations.preparation: Blend all ingredients, roll into a ball. No sugar needed.
food_recommendations.how_it_helps: Rich in healthy fats, iron, sugars. Supports fat increase, energy, hormonal balance.
food_recommendations.evidence: Asia Pacific Journal of Clinical Nutrition: Energy-dense snacks increase fat mass in low BMI.
